extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or advanced undergraduates in commutative algebra; readers working through Atiyah–Macdonald-style exercises and Math StackExchange contributors
extracted.subtask_description: Worked statements, equivalences and hints for exercises in a commutative-algebra chapter (localization, flatness, supports, primary decomposition, spectra/topologies, torsion modules). Provides statements to prove and short solution sketches/hints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units and localization equivalences
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalence of several conditions relating units in localizations S^{-1}A and T^{-1}A: x = t/1 in S^{-1}A is a unit iff φ(x) is a unit of T^{-1}A, and the chain of equivalences among statements (i)–(v) about when localization maps induce isomorphisms / when elements become units / existence of primes disjoint from multiplicative sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solution sketches show direct checking of inverses in localizations, using expressions a/s as inverses of t/1 and arguments about primes disjoint from S; references to previous exercise parts are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-divisors form union of prime ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of zero-divisors of a ring is a union of prime ideals (two proofs referenced: Exercise 1.14 and Exercise 3.7 of the book).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To show a minimal prime p consists of zero-divisors set S := A \ p and use maximality in a multiplicative set argument (Exercise 3.6). The notes sketch the contradiction argument if an element s0 ∈ S0 were not in S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal primes consist of zero-divisors (construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p is a minimal prime ideal then every element of p is a zero-divisor: set S := A \ p and use maximality in multiplicative sets to show S0 ⊂ S, leading to contradiction if not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument uses the maximality of S in the set Σ from Exercise 3.6 and the fact that adding an element outside S would generate a larger multiplicative set not containing 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization preserves absolute flatness
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) If A is absolutely flat and S is any multiplicatively closed subset, then S^{-1}A is absolutely flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show a = a^2 x implies a/s = (a/s)^2 (x/1) in localized ring; straightforward calculation with localization fractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of absolute flatness via localizations
rubrics_metrics.description: (ii) A is absolutely flat ⇐⇒ A_m is a field for each maximal ideal m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If A is absolutely flat then so are localizations; use earlier exercise that absolutely flat local ring is a field. Conversely, assume each A_m is a field; deduce (a^2)=(a) for all a by checking at maximal ideals, then apply Exercise 2.27 implication to conclude A absolutely flat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalences for A/N absolutely flat and spectral properties
rubrics_metrics.description: For ring A and nilradical N, the following are equivalent: (i) A/N is absolutely flat; (ii) every prime ideal of A is maximal; (iii) Spec(A) is a T1-space; (iv) Spec(A) is Hausdorff. Moreover, when satisfied, Spec(A) is compact and totally disconnected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs: show (iv)=> (iii) <=> (ii) easily. To get Hausdorff from primes maximal, construct a,b with ab=0 separating points; use multiplicative set S=(A\p_x)(A\p_y) and maximal ideal contraction contradictions. For compactness and total disconnectedness use that Xa is closed and that Xa are clopen in Hausdorff compact space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of Krull dimension ≤ 0
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalence among: (a) Krull dimension ≤ 0; (b) A/N absolutely flat; (c) for each a ∈ A the descending chain (a) ⊃ (a^2) ⊃ ··· stabilizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show (b)=> (c) by writing a = a^2 b and deriving stabilization of (a^n). Show (c)=> (a) by proving A/p is a field for any prime p (use an^{}(1-ab)=0 argument) hence primes maximal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torsion submodule facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and properties: torsion elements of M form submodule T(M); (i) M/T(M) is torsion-free, (ii) f(T(M)) ⊂ T(N) for module hom f: M→N, (iii) exactness of torsion functor in short exact sequences, (iv) T(M) is kernel of M → K ⊗_A M where K is field of fractions of domain A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: manipulate representatives and annihilators, use fraction module descriptions and direct limit descriptions of K to show vanishing of 1⊗x implies torsion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Torsion commutes with localization
rubrics_metrics.description: For integral domain A, module M and multiplicative S⊂A, T(S^{-1}M) = S^{-1}(T(M)). Equivalently: M torsion-free ⇔ M_p torsion-free for all primes p ⇔ M_m torsion-free for all maximals m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key identity Ann(x/s) = S^{-1}Ann(x) and use Proposition 3.14 to relate annihilators under localization; follow implications among (i),(ii),(iii) via localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nakayama-style local vanishing implies generation by ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is an A-module and a an ideal with M_m = 0 for all maximal ideals m ⊃ a, then M = aM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to showing (M/aM)_m=0 for each maximal m of A/a and use contraction of m to A and localization behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generators of free module are basis in A^n
rubrics_metrics.description: Every set of n generators of A^n is a basis of A^n; consequently every generating set of A^n has at least n elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct φ: A^n→A^n sending canonical basis to the generators; reduce to local case and show surjective endomorphism of free module over local ring is isomorphism (use Nakayama).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent conditions for faithful flatness
rubrics_metrics.description: For flat A-algebra B, the following are equivalent: (i) a_e c = a for all ideals a of A (extension-contraction equality); (ii) Spec(B)→Spec(A) surjective; (iii) for every maximal m of A we have mB ≠ (1); (iv) for every non-zero A-module M, M_B ≠ 0; (v) for every A-module M, the map M→M_B is injective. B faithful flat ⇔ these hold. Equivalent property (vi) for injectivity preserving under base change is also given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs relate extension/contraction, use Proposition 3.10 equivalences of flatness local criteria, and flatness/faithfully-flat exactness arguments. Hints outline (i)=> (ii), (iii)=>(iv), (iv)=>(v), (v)=>(i) and equivalence with (vi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness preserved under composition with faithfully flat map
rubrics_metrics.description: If A→B→C are ring homomorphisms with g∘f flat and g faithfully flat then f is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use criterion that injection M'→M remains injective after tensoring with B and then with C; faithful flatness of B→C lets one descend injectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surjectivity on spectra for localized flat maps
rubrics_metrics.description: If f: A→B is flat, q a prime of B and p = q^c, then f_* : Spec(B_q) → Spec(A_p) is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that localization and taking local rings preserve flatness and check condition (3) of Exercise 16 (characterization of faithful flatness) locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of a module and its basic properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and properties of Supp(M): (i) M ≠ 0 ⇔ Supp(M) ≠ ∅; (ii) V(a) = Supp(A/a); (iii) supports in short exact sequences decompose as union; (iv) support of direct sums is union of supports; (v) if M finitely generated then Supp(M)=V(Ann(M)); (vi) for finitely generated M,N, Supp(M⊗N)=Supp(M)∩Supp(N); (vii) Supp(M/aM)=V(a+Ann(M)) when M finitely generated; (viii) for f:A→B and finitely generated M, Supp(B⊗_A M)=f_*^{-1}(Supp(M)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: prove (iii),(iv) first; use Proposition 3.7 for tensor product support intersection; use finiteness and General Observation (reduce to cyclic modules A/a) to handle (v) and (vii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracted/extended primes and surjectivity/injectivity of f_*
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) Every prime of A is contracted ⇔ f_* is surjective. (ii) Every prime of B is extended ⇒ f_* is injective. Counterexample shows converse of (ii) need not hold (K→K[ε]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference Proposition 34; explicit counterexample provided: A=K, B=K[ε], shows injectivity of f_* can fail to imply all primes extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spec(S^{-1}A) homeomorphism onto image and fibers of f_*
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) For canonical φ:A→S^{-1}A, φ_*:Spec(S^{-1}A)→Spec(A) is homeomorphism onto its image S^{-1}X. (ii) For f:A→B and multiplicative S, S^{-1}f_* identifies with restriction of f_* to f_*^{-1}(S^{-1}X) and S^{-1}Y = f_*^{-1}(S^{-1}X). (iii) Passage to quotients: induced map between Spec(A/a) and Spec(B/b) is restriction of f_* to closed sets. (iv) Fiber over p is Spec(k(p)⊗_A B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use Proposition 3.11 about behavior of primes under localization, explicit checking of images, and the tensor description of fibers (Spec of base change to residue field).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection of basic open neighborhoods equals image of Spec(A_p)
rubrics_metrics.description: The canonical image of Spec(A_p) in Spec(A) equals the intersection of all open neighborhoods of p, equivalently {q | q ⊂ p} = ⋂_{f∉p} X_f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate verification using definitions of basic opens X_f and containment relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure sheaf on basic opens and restriction maps
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) For basic open U=X_f the ring A(U)=A_f depends only on U. (ii) If U'⊂U are basic opens X_g⊂X_f then there exists equation g^n = u f giving restriction hom Af→Ag by a/f^m ↦ a u^m / g^{mn}; this depends only on U,U'. (iii) identity when U=U'. (iv) restrictions compose. (v) Stalk at p is colimit of A(U) over U containing p and equals A_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the relationships among f and g when X_g⊂X_f to produce the homomorphism; (v) follows from colimit description of localization S^{-1}A as colim_{f∈S} A_f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing property: presheaf on basic opens is a sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: Given covering of X by basic opens (U_i) and sections s_i ∈ A(U_i) that agree on overlaps, there exists unique s∈A(X) whose restrictions equal s_i. (Hence presheaf is a sheaf.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct complex 0→A→∏A_{f_i}→∏A_{f_i f_j} and show exactness; reduce to local case where one generator is unit, then check injectivity and exactness directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image of spectrum under tensor product map
rubrics_metrics.description: For maps f:A→B and g:A→C and h:A→B⊗_A C defined by h(x)=f(x)⊗g(x), we have h_*(Spec(B⊗_A C)) = f_*(Spec(B)) ∩ g_*(Spec(C)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work fiberwise: p∈h_*(T) iff (B⊗_A k(p))⊗_k(p)(C⊗_A k(p)) ≠ 0, equivalent to both B⊗_A k(p) and C⊗_A k(p) nonzero; use Exercise 3.21iv for fiber description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructible topology and XC properties
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) For each g∈A, X_g is both open and closed in constructible topology. (ii) The topology C generated by making X_g clopen makes X_C Hausdorff. (iii) Identity X→X_C is a homeomorphism; subsets that are images f_*(Spec(B)) are exactly C-closed sets. (iv) X_C is compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show X_g closed in constructible topology (closed under finite unions/intersections of basic constructible sets); separate distinct primes using some X_g and V(g); combine with compactness of constructible topology to deduce total disconnectedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zariski equals constructible topology ⇔ A/N absolutely flat
rubrics_metrics.description: The Zariski and constructible topologies on Spec(A) coincide iff A/N is absolutely flat (N nilradical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use equivalence that identity map X→X_C is homeomorphism iff X is Hausdorff, and earlier equivalence between X Hausdorff and A/N absolutely flat (Exercise 3.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracted primary ideal need not be contraction of primary ideal (counterexample)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist contracted primary ideals in a subring which are not contractions of any primary ideal of an overring. Example: A=K[ε] with ε^2=0 embedded in specially constructed B (K[x,y_i...]/relations) where (0)⊂A is contracted primary but not contraction of a primary ideal of B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction embeds ε as x y1 with relations forcing ε∈(x^n) for all n; show any primary q of B must contain ε so contraction is (1) not (0). Reference Math.SE solution by user26857.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence of primary ideals under localization
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiplicative S and decomposable ideal a=∩_i q_i minimal primary decomposition, number primes so S meets p_{m+1},...,p_n but not p_1,...,p_m; then S^{-1}a = ∩_{i=1}^m S^{-1}q_i and S(a)=∩_{i=1}^m q_i. A primary ideal of A is contracted iff its radical is disjoint from S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contraction and extension maps between primary ideals of A and S^{-1}A are inverse bijections onto those whose radicals are disjoint from S; use Proposition 3.11 and Proposition 3.14 facts about localization preserving primarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second Uniqueness Theorem (isolated primary components independence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a be decomposable with minimal primary decomposition a=∩_{i=1}^n q_i and let {p_{i1},...,p_{im}} be an isolated set of prime ideals of a. Then q_{i1}∩...∩q_{im} is independent of the decomposition (isolated primary components uniquely determined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary: isolated primary components (those corresponding to minimal primes) are uniquely determined; proofs refer to Theorem 4.5 uniqueness arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of non-decomposable ideals via idealization
rubrics_metrics.description: The idealization (trivial extension) A=R×M can produce ideals with finitely many minimal primes but no primary decomposition; e.g., ideal {0}×Z in idealization of Q over Z has only one minimal prime but no primary decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List properties of idealization (ideals containing {0}×M correspond to ideals of R, prime ideals are p×M, etc.) and cite Math.SE examples showing {0}×Z lacks primary decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: If A absolutely flat then primary ideals are maximal and converse
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise and corollary facts: (i) If A absolutely flat then every primary ideal is maximal. (ii) Converse: if all primary ideals are prime (PP rings) then A is absolutely flat (local reductions and cases argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs: For (i) show nonzero a leads to unit or nilpotent contradiction. For converse, reduce to local PP rings and analyze cases (single prime, domain with finite generation arguments, etc.) following Math.SE reference by wxu.
